title: Underwriting Guide: Cardinal Rental Reimbursement Option Eligibility Table
content:
Personal Auto Underwriting rates Cardinal Rental Reimbursement as an option on one scheduled vehicle. Two things limit which option a vehicle may carry: the physical damage on the vehicle, and the highest rental option rank that the household's Cardinal Personal Auto Policy package allows.

## Entry requirements by option

| Option | Rank | Package must allow a rental option rank of at least | Requires physical damage on the same vehicle |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 30/900 | 1 | 1 | Yes |
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 40/1200 | 2 | 2 | Yes |
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 50/1500 | 3 | 3 | Yes |
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 60/1800 | 4 | 4 | Yes |
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 75/2250 | 5 | 5 | Yes |
| Cardinal Rental Reimbursement 100/3000 | 6 | 6 | Yes |

## How the option relates to other coverage, by option

| Term | 30/900 | 40/1200 | 50/1500 | 60/1800 | 75/2250 | 100/3000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Suspended while the vehicle's physical damage is in storage | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Rental moves to the at-fault party's insurer once that insurer accepts liability | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Unearned option premium returned on removal | Pro rata | Pro rata | Pro rata | Pro rata | Pro rata | Pro rata |

## Reading the table (hypothetical)

- A package whose highest allowed rental option rank is 4 meets the entry requirement of 30/900, 40/1200, 50/1500 and 60/1800. It does not meet the requirement of 75/2250 (rank 5) or 100/3000 (rank 6).
- A package whose highest allowed rank is 6 meets the requirement of every option.
- A vehicle insured for liability alone does not meet the physical damage requirement of any option.
- An option removed with 40% of its term unexpired returns 40% of its full-term premium, because unearned premium is returned pro rata.
